note: Autumn clocks (IEM ASOS 2021–2025, diurnal days) in ET. Summer shows the median only.

cards.name: Miami Intl
cards.quirk: A sea-breeze clock: the median peak is 12:53 PM, earliest in the East. The high is often set before lunch; the afternoon is defense.

cards.name: Newark Liberty Intl
cards.quirk: The earliest window on the East board — p10 at 11:51 AM ET. Newark's peak hour arrives before New York's.

cards.name: Boston Logan Intl
cards.quirk: Logan sits on the water: the sea breeze can cap the high by early afternoon, and 9.5% of autumn days top out before 9 AM entirely.

cards.name: Trenton-Mercer
cards.quirk: Fifty miles from Newark, a full hour behind it: a 2:50 PM median makes Trenton the late station of the New Jersey pair.

cards.name: Central Park
cards.quirk: Central Park prints HOURLY, plus special reports — the only station of the 24 with no 5-minute stream. If your weather app shows a new New York high before the station prints it, the app is guessing.

cards.name: Reagan National
cards.quirk: The steadiest Eastern clock: the 2 PM hour takes 35% of days, and the East's lowest frontal share (4.9%).

cards.name: Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson
cards.quirk: The South's long tail — only 55.5% of highs are set by 3 PM local and the window runs to 4:52 PM ET. Atlanta rewards patience.

cards.name: Houston Hobby
cards.quirk: Hobby, not Bush Intercontinental. The bay breeze leans it early: median 1:53 PM local, window shut by 3:53.

cards.name: Chicago Midway
cards.quirk: Midway, not O'Hare — and a lake-breeze station besides. 13.4% of autumn days max before 9 AM, the Midwest's most frontal profile after Minneapolis.

cards.name: Los Angeles Intl
cards.quirk: The earliest peak in America: median 11:53 AM local, 99.0% of highs set by 3 PM. The sea breeze shuts the day down by lunch.

cards.name: Philadelphia Intl
cards.quirk: A late tail for an Eastern station — a quarter of autumn highs are still unset at 3 PM local.

cards.name: Louisville Intl
cards.quirk: Frontal share of 10.5% and the latest Eastern window (to 4:56 PM ET) — Louisville can go either way, and go late.

cards.name: New Orleans Intl (Moisant)
cards.quirk: Early-leaning Gulf: a 2:29 PM median. Gulf moisture caps the climb sooner than at the other Central stations.

cards.name: San Diego Intl
cards.quirk: Sea-breeze early and tidy: a 12:51 PM median, and every autumn high in five years of sample was set by 5 PM local.

cards.name: Oklahoma City (Will Rogers)
cards.quirk: The earliest honest start in the Central group: its p10 (1:44 PM local) beats every neighbor's.

cards.name: Austin-Bergstrom Intl
cards.quirk: Standard-late Texas: a 2:53 PM median and a window to 4:53 PM local. Austin cooks a long afternoon.

cards.name: Dallas/Fort Worth Intl
cards.quirk: A metronome when the air mass holds — the 2 PM hour takes 37% of days, and 99.6% of highs are set by 5 PM local.

cards.name: Minneapolis-St. Paul Intl
cards.quirk: The most frontal station on the board: 14.1% of autumn days print their high before 9 AM. On a front day, the peak window never happens.

cards.name: San Antonio Intl
cards.quirk: The latest median in America in autumn — 3:35 PM local. San Antonio's high is an end-of-day event.

cards.name: Phoenix Sky Harbor
cards.quirk: The most predictable station in the system: 0.7% early-max days and 100% of highs set by 5 PM local. Arizona skips daylight saving, so its ET clock shifts an hour earlier after Nov 1.

cards.name: Denver Intl
cards.quirk: The window opens before noon local (p10 11:53 AM) — high-plains sun does its work early.

cards.name: Seattle-Tacoma Intl
cards.quirk: The widest window on the board — 11:53 AM to 4:53 PM local. Marine air makes Seattle's peak the hardest to time.

cards.name: San Francisco Intl
cards.quirk: Marine-layer variable: the median says 2:22 PM, but the layer decides — when it burns off late, the peak comes late.

cards.name: Las Vegas (Harry Reid) Intl
cards.quirk: Desert late but disciplined: a 2:56 PM median, and 99.7% of highs set by 5 PM local.
